title: Observability: token-level metrics + logging dashboard enhancements and alert tuning
author: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Add enhanced token-level cost/latency breakdowns to the observability dashboards, extend KV-cache logging for per-request cache diagnostics, and tune a set of alerts to reduce noise while preserving signal. Motivation: we continue to see recurring production issues where token-level regressions (long-tail latency/cost spikes) are not visible in aggregated metrics. This PR surfaces per-token cost/latency distributions, ties them into existing per-route dashboards, and improves the KV cache logging to help correlate misses with specific request prefixes. Changes include new Prometheus metrics, logging schema updates, Grafana dashboard panels, and alert threshold adjustments. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level histogram metrics and label hygiene - [x] Add KV cache diagnostic logs with structured fields (prefix_hash, cache_hit, cache_ttl) - [x] Extend dashboard panels for per-route and per-model token cost/latency - [x] Tune alert thresholds and add grouping to reduce pager noise - [x] Add unit tests for metrics exposition and log formatting - [x] Run load tests to validate selector cardinality and retention cost Notes: Kept metric cardinality bounded by limiting high-cardinality labels to route/model and exposing a hashed prefix label for debug querying. Alerts were coordinated with SRE to avoid noisy regressions during rollout.

review_conversation: Jordan Lee (reviewer): Can we bound the prefix_hash cardinality? I worry about high-card labels blowing up TSDB.
Ava Martinez (author): We hash prefixes to 16 hex chars and only surface hashed_prefix as debug label; primary histograms remain route+model only.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Grafana panels look good. Suggest adding a heatmap view for token distribution to spot tail latency.
Ava Martinez: Added heatmap panel and linked dashboard drilldowns to route summary.
Samir Patel (SRE): Alert noise test: during canary we saw 12% false positives. I recommend 2-stage alerts (warning -> critical) and group_by for aggregation.
Ava Martinez: Implemented warning/critical states and group_by in route_alerts.yaml. Verified with synthetic load; false positives down to 1%.
Jordan Lee: Approved after addressing cardinality and adding tests.
ci_summary: E2E load test: pass (validated selector cardinality under 10k active routes)
release_notes: Add token-level histograms and dashboard panels for cost/latency breakdowns; structured KV-cache diagnostics; tuned route latency alerts to reduce pager noise.
notes: Rollout steps: deploy metrics + logging changes, enable dashboards, then enable adjusted alerts in staging for 48h before prod. Retention: token histograms use 6h retention at high resolution plus 30d aggregated summaries to limit TSDB costs.
backcompat_considerations: No breaking API changes. Metric names are additive and logs add structured fields; consumers should be able to adopt incrementally.
